name: Upper-Root-Locked Pairs Have a Canonical One-Hole Normal Form
statement: For oriented one-hole data $(y,S)$, let $\mathsf P(y,S)=\{y^T:\varnothing\ne T\subseteq S\}$ be the punctured cube and $\mathsf I(y,S)=\{y^T:T\subseteq S, |T|\ge2\}$ its interior. Given $A$ and a finite family $\mathcal W$ of such data, put $B(A,\mathcal W)=A\cup\bigcup_{(y,S)\in\mathcal W}\mathsf P(y,S)$. If $A$ and $B(A,\mathcal W)$ satisfy Sandwich equality, every tip $y$ is absent, the relative part is nonempty, and every relative concept lies in one of the displayed interiors, then $A\subsetneq B(A,\mathcal W)$ is an upper-root-locked nested ample pair. Conversely, every upper-root-locked nested ample pair $A\subsetneq B$ has this form. It is canonically recovered by taking all absent-tip punctured cubes $\mathsf P(y,S)\subseteq B$ whose interiors meet $B\setminus A$ and whose supports are inclusion-maximal for their fixed tips. Thus upper-root-locked relative Yang presentations have an explicit descendant-free construction and recovery.
proof: The Sandwich equalities make both endpoint families ample. If a relative concept $x=y^T$ lies in a displayed interior, then $|T|\ge2$, every proper flip $x^C$ with $C\subsetneq T$ lies in the punctured cube, and the full flip $x^T=y$ is absent. Hence $T$ is a nontrivial minimal nonface of the local cube-support complex at $x$; $x$ is not a corner, so deleting it makes $B$ nonample. This proves upper-root-locking. Conversely, upper-root-locking makes every relative $x$ a noncorner of $B$. A minimal nonface $S$ of its local cube-support complex supplies an absent tip $y=x^S$ with $\mathsf P(y,S)\subseteq B$ and $x\in\mathsf I(y,S)$. Extending $S$ maximally for its fixed tip yields the canonical family, protects every relative concept, and reconstructs exactly $B$.
comments: The admissibility test uses only finite Sandwich equalities, missing tips, and punctured-cube containment; it contains no deletion, corner, shelling, linear-quotient, or rooted-connectivity predicate. This classifies individual upper-locked pairs, while compatibility of two such covers over a common overlap remains separate.
